question: The Aditya L-1 mission of ISRO was launched in which of the following year?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2023**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__
 __ 
• The **Aditya L-1 mission** was launched by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** in the year **2023**. 
• The mission is India's first dedicated solar observation mission, aimed at studying the **Sun's corona, chromosphere, and solar winds**. 
• Aditya L-1 was launched on **September 2, 2023**, using the **PSLV-C57** rocket from the **Sriharikota spaceport**. 
• The spacecraft is designed to be placed in a **halo orbit around the Lagrange Point 1 (L1)** of the Sun-Earth system, approximately **1.5 million kilometers** from Earth. 
• The mission aims to provide crucial information about **solar activities** and their impact on Earth's **space weather** systems. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Aditya L-1 Mission Objectives:** 
• To study the dynamics of the **solar corona**, which is the outermost layer of the Sun's atmosphere. 
• To understand the processes behind the **solar wind** and its interaction with the Earth's magnetosphere. 
• To observe the **photosphere and chromosphere** of the Sun and analyze their behavior. 
• To monitor **solar flares** and coronal mass ejections (CMEs) that influence space weather. 
• To investigate particle behavior in the Earth's vicinity caused by solar activities. 
• **Lagrange Point 1 (L1):** 
• Lagrange Point 1 (L1) is a stable location in space where the gravitational forces of the Sun and Earth balance the orbital motion of a satellite. 
• It allows continuous observation of the Sun without interruptions caused by Earth's rotation or other celestial movements. 
• The L1 point is located approximately **1.5 million kilometers** from Earth in the direction of the Sun. 
• **Scientific Instruments on Aditya L-1:** 
• **Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC):** Designed to study the solar corona and measure its magnetic field. 
• **Solar Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope (SUIT):** Observes the photosphere and chromosphere in ultraviolet wavelengths. 
• **Aditya Solar Wind Particle Experiment (ASPEX):** Studies solar wind particles and their properties. 
• **Plasma Analyser Package for Aditya (PAPA):** Analyzes plasma in the solar wind. 
• **Significance of Aditya L-1:** 
• It is India's first solar observation mission, marking a major milestone in space research. 
• The data collected will help scientists better understand **space weather phenomena**, which can impact satellite operations and communication systems. 
• It contributes to global efforts in studying the Sun, alongside missions like NASA's **Parker Solar Probe** and ESA's **Solar Orbiter**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **PSLV-C57 Rocket:** 
• The Aditya L-1 mission was launched using the **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV)**, a trusted workhorse of ISRO. 
• PSLV-C57 ensured precise placement of the spacecraft in its intended trajectory toward the L1 point. 
• **Space Weather Impact:** 
• Space weather events, such as solar storms, can disrupt **satellite communication, navigation systems, and power grids**. 
• Understanding these phenomena is crucial for mitigating their effects on technological systems. 
• **Global Collaborations:** 
• Aditya L-1 complements international missions like NASA's **Parker Solar Probe**, which studies the Sun's atmosphere and solar wind. 
• Such missions contribute to a collective understanding of the Sun and its influence on the solar system. </ul
